disease_label_per_paper: Postpartum thrombotic microangiopathy revealed as atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome successfully treated with eculizumab
presentation_summary: A previously healthy 23-year-old woman underwent urgent cesarean section at 31 weeks for preeclampsia with nephrotic-range proteinuria, blood pressure 180/100 mmHg, and edema.
Five days after cesarean section she developed hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, renal impairment, tonicoclonic seizures, and hypertensive crisis.
Initial reported TMA labs included schistocytes, LDH 3254 IU/L, total bilirubin 4.2 mg/dL, creatinine 4.9 mg/dL, and platelet count 40 x10^9/L.
Intensive plasma exchange twice daily and dialysis were started; she transiently improved but relapsed months later with renal failure and recurrent TMA manifestations.

Later workup showed detectable ADAMTS13 activity, negative Shiga toxin/E. coli stool testing, and kidney biopsy evidence of progressive TMA; eculizumab controlled recurrent TMA after relapse during interruption.

risk_context.source_text_value: 31-week pregnant young woman; five days post-cesarean section
urgent cesarean section due to preeclampsia presenting with nephrotic-range proteinuria, increased blood pressure, and edema

observations.source_text_value: hypertensive crisis with seizures and renal impairment
Schistocytes were detected on her peripheral blood smear
dialysis for volume and uremia control

course_observations.source_text_value: Following PE and dialysis her clinical condition transiently improved (serum creatinine: 2.8mg/dL, LDH: 605IU/L, PLT: 141 x10^9/L)
PLT: 141 x10^9/L after PE and dialysis
Approximately four months later ... serum creatinine 8mg/dL
last follow-up visit on May 2013 ... creatinine level, 1.5mg/dL

cardiac_observations.source_text_value: left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) via transthoracic echocardiography: 35 to 40 percent
pulmonary hypertension: right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP): 47.1mmHg
cardiac function was improved (LVEF: 45 to 50 percent)

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: diagnosed with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome
Stool samples could not detect Escherichia coli O157:H7/O104:H4 or Shiga toxin
kidney biopsy ... revealed evidence of progressing TMA with excessive neutrophil infiltrations, capillary loop blockade occlusions and abnormal capillary wall thickening

confirmatory_findings.finding: Eculizumab response and relapse on interruption
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: transient pause in treatment resulted in thrombotic microangiopathy relapse, which was rapidly blocked with reintroduction of eculizumab treatment

actual_treatment: intensive plasma exchange twice daily for 22 days
dialysis for volume and uremia control
restarted plasma exchange and dialysis after relapse
eculizumab 900 mg weekly for four weeks followed by 1200 mg dose
eculizumab reintroduction at 900 mg then 1200 mg every two weeks
antibiotics, diuretics, and antihypertensives during pneumonia/cardiac failure admission

outcome.renal_outcome: non-dialysis dependent with creatinine 1.5 mg/dL at last follow-up
outcome.cardiac_outcome: LVEF improved to 45-50 percent and pulmonary pressure normalized
outcome.source_text_value: free of any TMA-related complications; no PE/PI, no dialysis and no blood transfusions were necessary

quality_warnings: ADAMTS13, stool Shiga toxin/E. coli testing, renal biopsy, eculizumab response, and paper diagnosis are confirmatory/context evidence with use_in_ranking:false.
Presentation hemoglobin was described as hemolytic anemia but no exact initial value was reported, so no presentation hemoglobin observation was fabricated.
Later treatment-response and relapse labs are retained in course_observations with use_in_ranking:false.
